label: input token f at original positions 0-3
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is the letter f at one of the first four original-phase steps (t = 0..3). It fires on every such step: no false positives on dev. Position sets the magnitude. f at t=0 reaches about 0.91 of max, f at t=1 reaches about 0.85-1.0 (1.0 when t=0 was also f), f at t=2 reaches about 0.85-0.9, and f at t=3 drops to about 0.4. It does not fire on f at original positions 4 and later, on the delimiter, or on copy-phase inputs, even when the fed-back input is f. It does not fire on other tokens apart from a negligible trace (about 0.02 of max, 0.1% of mass) on y/m/n/v right after an initial f.

issues: Minor overclaim. The explanation says the feature never fires on copy-phase inputs, even when the fed-back input is f. In fact it fires weakly (about 0.04-0.11 of max) on 64 dev steps. All of them are L=3 sequences with f at original position 1, at step 5, where the fed-back input is f. That is 0.006% of activation mass, so it does not matter in practice, but the 'never' wording is slightly too strong.

The predicate has zero false positives on the test split (precision 1). The 2,327 test steps it misses hold only 0.1% of mass. All of them are the claimed trace of about 0.02 of max on y/m/n/v right after an initial f, so no systematic gap remains.
Profile checks: no activation at t>=4 in the original phase or on the delimiter. Activation mass by t (0.29/0.31/0.27/0.125) matches the claim that t=3 is weaker.
